/* Tier-2 C-level round-trip smoke test.
 *
 * Phase 1 (QEMU1): printf via newlib stdio -> libgloss_vh -> semihosting,
 *   handled by QEMU. Then slti x0, x0,  0x5A0 -- plugin drains state.
 * Phase 2 (vsim):  empty body. Phase-2 rule (rt_c_helpers.h): no syscall
 *   may issue inside this span.
 * Phase 3 (QEMU2): printf again, then crt0 calls _exit(0) -> libgloss_vh
 *   semihosting SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED.
 */

#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
  printf("hello from QEMU1\n");
  fflush(stdout);

  enter_vsim();
  /* Phase 2: vsim. No syscalls. */
  exit_vsim();

  printf("hello from QEMU2\n");
  fflush(stdout);
  return 0;
}

=== CURRENT rt_c_helpers.h ===
/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
 *
 * Phase rule:
 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
 *   to register/memory work only.
 *
 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers: the HINT pair
 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
 *
 * Each helper exposes a global `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` label co-located
 * with the marker insn. The labels are inert in marker mode and consumed by
 * the PC-trigger mode driver (resolved via `nm --defined-only`). Because
 * each fixture calls each helper exactly once, the labels stay unique. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_enter_pc\n"
                       "_hybrid_enter_pc:\n"
                       "slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_exit_pc\n"
                       "_hybrid_exit_pc:\n"
                       "slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

2	 *
3	 * Phase rule:
4	 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
5	 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
6	 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
7	 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
8	 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
9	 *   to register/memory work only.
10	 *
11	 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
12	 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
13	 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
14	 */

16	#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
17	#define RT_C_HELPERS_H
18	
19	/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers: the HINT pair
20	 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
21	 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
22	 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
23	 *
24	 * Each helper exposes a global `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` label co-located
25	 * with the marker insn. The labels are inert in marker mode and consumed by
26	 * the PC-trigger mode driver (resolved via `nm --defined-only`). Because
27	 * each fixture calls each helper exactly once, the labels stay unique. */
28	/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
29	 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
30	 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
31	 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
32	 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
33	 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
34	 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
35	 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
36	/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
37	 *
38	 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
39	 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
40	 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
41	 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
42	 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
43	 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
44	 * consumes the value.)
45	 *
46	 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
47	 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
48	 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
49	 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
50	 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
51	 *     between the markers.
52	 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
53	 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
54	 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
55	 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
56	 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
57	 * attribution. */
58	static inline void enter_vsim(void)
59	{
60	  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_enter_pc\n"
61	                       "_hybrid_enter_pc:\n"
62	                       "slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
63	}
64	static inline void exit_vsim(void)
65	{
66	  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_exit_pc\n"
67	                       "_hybrid_exit_pc:\n"
68	                       "slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
69	}
